answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A velvet delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A gale check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A voyage penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 3097 identities need 3097 bonds of 63 tokens, 27059 dollars of hardware and 42 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
